channel.title: HistoryPulse — The Uncut Story
channel.description: Deep-dive uncut narrations from real historical sources.
channel.itunes:author: HistoryPulse

item.title: The Day the Birds Fell from the Sky
item.description: Krishna Deva Raya breaks a forty-year peace with the Adil Shah of Bijapur after a trusted Moor named Cide Mercar absconds to the Sultan's court with forty thousand gold pardaos. He marches a million-strong army on the fortress city of Raichur, fights a battle so loud that birds fall from the sky, sees his front line shattered by Bijapur's massed artillery, sends a ring to his queens as token of his death — and then turns the rout into a total massacre by ordering his cavalry to kill his own fleeing men. Based on A Forgotten Empire (Vijayanagara) by Robert Sewell (1900), drawing on the chronicle of Fernão Nuniz.

item.title: The Goat's Eyes: How a Minister's Trick Saved Krishna Deva Raya and Forged an Empire
item.description: In this episode, the dying king Busbalrao orders his minister Salvatimya to blind his brother Krishna Deva Raya and place his eight-year-old son on the throne. Salvatimya saves Krishna by substituting a goat's eyes, and the young prince rises to become one of India's greatest kings — launching a devastating eastern campaign that captures Udayagiri after an eighteen-month siege, crushes the Gajapati army at a river crossing, and takes Kondapalli, where the Orissan prince kills himself rather than duel a commoner. Based on A Forgotten Empire (Vijayanagara) by Robert Sewell (1900).

item.title: The Bleeding Throne: Fratricide, Usurpation, and the Death of the First Dynasty
item.description: Chapter 6 chronicles the violent implosion of Vijayanagara's first dynasty across four decades of fratricide, military losses, and systemic decay. Following Deva Raya the Second, the empire cycled through weak and murderous kings — sons killing fathers, brothers slaughtering brothers — while the Bahmani sultanate seized the western ports and a massacre of Muslim merchants at Bhatkal accidentally seeded the founding of Goa. The dynasty ends not with a foreign invasion but with a general named Narasimha, whose captain walks through unguarded city gates, enters an empty palace, and seizes the throne as the last king flees into the dark. Based on A Forgotten Empire (Vijayanagara) by Robert Sewell (1900).

item.title: The House of Slaughter — How a Brother's Trap Nearly Destroyed the Greatest Hindu Empire
item.description: In 1443, the brother of King Deva Raya II of Vijayanagara orchestrated one of medieval India's most chilling assassinations — luring the empire's nobles one by one into a newly built house where assassins butchered them behind a wall of deafening drums, then attacking the king himself with a hidden dagger. Deva Raya survived by fighting back with his own throne and escaping through the harem, but the massacre gutted the empire's leadership, and the ensuing war with the Bahmani Sultan Ala-ud-din cost the king his eldest son and forced him into a humiliating tribute agreement. Based on A Forgotten Empire (Vijayanagara) by Robert Sewell (1900), drawing on the accounts of Abdur Razzak and Firishtah.

item.title: The King Who Fled in Sugarcane: Deva Raya II and the Edge of Extinction
item.description: In this chapter, Deva Raya II transforms the Vijayanagara Empire through bitter experience and radical reform. After a shocking battlefield assassination turns the tide against Sultan Firuz, the new Bahmani Sultan Ahmad Shah launches a devastating invasion that catches Deva Raya sleeping in a garden, forcing him to flee disguised as a laborer carrying sugarcane. Ahmad's genocidal rampage provokes a desperate Hindu suicide squad of five thousand warriors who nearly kill the sultan in a mud cattle pen, but the king is ultimately forced into humiliating surrender, sending his own son with treasure-laden elephants to kneel at the sultan's feet. Years later, Deva Raya asks the revolutionary question of why his larger, richer empire keeps losing — and the answer leads him to recruit Muslims into Hindu service, build a mosque in Vijayanagara, and place a Quran before his own throne, creating a reformed military machine that would preserve the empire for generations. Based on A Forgotten Empire (Vijayanagara) by Robert Sewell (1900).

item.title: Blood on the Dance Floor: Assassination, Invasion, and a King Undone by Love — Vijayanagara Empire Chapter 3
item.description: In this chapter, we witness the brutal succession struggles of the Bahmani Sultanate — where boy-kings are blinded within weeks of taking the throne — and the dramatic assassination of Bukka II's son by a Bahmani spy named Cauzi Serauje, who infiltrated the Hindu camp disguised as a musician during a night entertainment, charmed the prince with his playing, then plunged daggers into his breast during a knife dance. The ensuing chaos allowed Sultan Firuz Shah to cross the flooded Krishna River and rout the Vijayanagar army, leading to a humiliating peace treaty. We then follow the reckless King Deva Raya I, whose obsessive desire for a farmer's beautiful daughter named Pertal — a girl who courageously refused his proposal — drove him to launch a military raid into Bahmani territory, sparking a catastrophic war that ended with the unprecedented disgrace of giving a Hindu princess in marriage to a Muslim sultan. Based on A Forgotten Empire (Vijayanagara) by Robert Sewell (1900).

item.title: Blood on the Tungabhadra: When Total War Came to Vijayanagara
item.description: Sultan Muhammad Shah Bahmani launches total war against Vijayanagara in 1366, inflicting catastrophic defeats on Bukka Raya — including a massacre at the Tungabhadra battlefield where even pregnant women and infants were slaughtered, and a devastating night attack that caught the king drinking with dancing-women — ultimately claiming 500,000 Hindu lives before peace is bought. Years later, the young Sultan Mujahid penetrates to the very heart of the capital and destroys a sacred jeweled temple, only to be assassinated by his own uncle Daud Khan, whose treachery gives Bukka the opening to reclaim the disputed Doab territories. Based on "A Forgotten Empire (Vijayanagara)" by Robert Sewell (1900).

item.title: The City of Victory: How Two Captured Brothers Built an Empire from the Ashes — Vijayanagara, Chapter 1
item.description: In this opening chapter, we trace the cataclysmic events that led to the founding of Vijayanagara around 1336 CE — from the relentless southward advance of the Delhi Sultanate under rulers like Ala-ud-din Khilji and the terrifying Muhammad Taghlaq, through the fall of the Hindu fortress of Kampli-Anegundi, to the rise of two brothers, Harihara and Bukka, who — guided by the sage Vidyaranya — established a new city on the Tungabhadra River that would become the last great Hindu empire of southern India. Based on A Forgotten Empire (Vijayanagara) by Robert Sewell (1900).
